patients.email is health data; out of scope for a customer-email audit

The customer approved the plan in the brief; I did not change the AI loop or webhook retry behaviour, only proposed them
statement.containment with object_kinds [task] for api.request is an acceptable proxy for retry-forever, as the customer's task is a while loop
confusions: Template audit_log_protected's write_location_restricted: unclear whether omitting statements gives every built-in write (I assumed yes, which is what the dry run accepted, but no evaluate was run to confirm)
Recipe 'Record who changed what' gives db.edit, db.patch, db.del rules but no guidance for db.add (creates); I added db.add myself

Whether an object.statement_required rule should cover function objects: the catalogue's kind list excludes functions, so writes inside functions are unjudged by that check even though the recipe implies coverage
Whether a table-level tag was needed for scope: I scoped by exact table names instead, as the skill suggests when the user names tables

Policy check result is not visible from dry-run: the dry run lists policy create lines but no findings, so I cannot confirm the rules judge anything until evaluate runs (which the brief forbids for me)

Parse warnings about names that the branch does not have yet are expected when the change creates them, but the skill's rule is 'never accept the warning'; the warnings here are for objects this change creates
